cl_gen_gabapentinoids.q: Can you get addicted to gabapentin or Lyrica, and is it risky?
cl_gen_gabapentinoids.short: Yes, mostly people with opioid or other drug problems. In a German detox ward, 11 in 100 who'd used Lyrica were dependent on it. Deaths nearly always involved other drugs.
cl_gen_gabapentinoids.but: Nearly all the studies were of people who already had drug problems. How often anyone else becomes dependent hasn't been measured.
how: In a German detox ward where everyone was already dependent on other drugs, 56 in 100 had used Lyrica. Of those, 11 in 100 met the criteria for dependence.

Misuse is far more common in people with opioid problems. Among 250 former prisoners, 26 in 100 with an opioid problem said they'd misused gabapentin, against 4 in 100 without. In one online survey of the public, about 1 in 100 had.

Case reports often describe tolerance and withdrawal, sometimes with seizures. Of 55 published cases, only 4 people, all on Lyrica, had craving or loss of control without an earlier drug problem. Case reports can't show how often that happens.
Deaths with these medicines nearly always involved other drugs, mostly opioids. In a Swedish study, overdoses weren't more common after a prescription once people with drug problems were left out.
cl_gen_gabapentinoids.rate: Two reviews that didn't check the quality of the studies they gathered, mostly of people with drug problems, plus case reports. The figures are second-hand, and nothing here shows the medicines caused the deaths.

general.statement: Gabapentin and Lyrica aren't opioids, so stopping them can't cause withdrawal.
general.why: Case reports often describe tolerance and withdrawal, sometimes with seizures. They're case reports, so they can't show how common it is.

prescription-opioids.statement: Deaths involving gabapentin or Lyrica usually involve those medicines alone.
prescription-opioids.why: Deaths with them nearly always involved other drugs too, mostly opioids. That alone doesn't show which drug caused a death.
